questions.prompt: Using the method of joints, determine the force in member $BC$ of the truss shown ($84\text{-kN}$ load at $B$; pin at $A$, roller against the wall at $C$). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
Geometry: $B(0,\,4)$, $A(3,\,5.25)$, $C(3,\,0)\,\text{m}$. Then $BA = \sqrt{3^2 + 1.25^2} = 3.25\,\text{m}$ and $BC = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\,\text{m}$.

**Joint B** (assume both members in tension, forces pointing away from $B$):

$$\xrightarrow{+}\sum F_x = 0:\quad \tfrac{3}{3.25}F_{AB} + \tfrac{3}{5}F_{BC} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{AB} = -0.65F_{BC}$$

$$+\!\uparrow\sum F_y = 0:\quad \tfrac{1.25}{3.25}F_{AB} - \tfrac{4}{5}F_{BC} - 84 = 0$$

Substituting: $-0.25F_{BC} - 0.80F_{BC} = 84 \Rightarrow F_{BC} = -80.0\,\text{kN}$.

The negative sign means member $BC$ pushes on the joint: $F_{BC} = 80.0\,\text{kN}\;C$. (Also $F_{AB} = 52.0\,\text{kN}\;T$, and from joint $C$, $F_{AC} = 64.0\,\text{kN}\;T$.)

questions.prompt: Determine the force in member $AB$ of the Pratt roof truss shown ($5.7\,\text{kN}$ at $A$ and $H$, $10.5\,\text{kN}$ at $B$ and $F$, $9.6\,\text{kN}$ at $D$; pin at $A$, roller at $H$; rise $2.4\,\text{m}$). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
**Reactions.** Total load $= 2(5.7) + 2(10.5) + 9.6 = 42.0\,\text{kN}$. By symmetry $A_y = H = 21.0\,\text{kN}\uparrow$.

**Geometry.** The rafter $ABD$ rises $2.4\,\text{m}$ over $7.0\,\text{m}$. For $AB$ (horizontal run $3.8\,\text{m}$, rise $3.8(2.4/7) = 1.303\,\text{m}$, length $4.017\,\text{m}$): $\sin = 0.3244$, $\cos = 0.9459$.

**Joint A.** The net upward force from the support and the joint load is $21.0 - 5.7 = 15.3\,\text{kN}$.

$$+\!\uparrow\sum F_y = 0:\quad 15.3 + 0.3244F_{AB} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{AB} = -47.2\,\text{kN}$$

$$\xrightarrow{+}\sum F_x = 0:\quad F_{AC} + 0.9459(-47.2) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{AC} = 44.6\,\text{kN}\;T$$

So $F_{AB} = 47.2\,\text{kN}\;C$.

questions.prompt: For the Pratt roof truss shown, determine the force in the diagonal member $CD$. Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
**Joint B.** Members $AB$ and $BD$ are collinear. The only other forces are the $10.5\text{-kN}$ load and member $BC$, both vertical. Summing components perpendicular to $ABD$ shows that $BC$ must balance the load: $F_{BC} = 10.50\,\text{kN}\;C$, and $F_{BD} = F_{AB} = 47.2\,\text{kN}\;C$.

**Joint C** (members $CA$, $CB$, $CD$, $CE$; no load). Diagonal $CD$ runs $3.2\,\text{m}$ across and $2.4\,\text{m}$ up (length $4.0\,\text{m}$), so it has components $(0.8,\,0.6)$.

$$+\!\uparrow\sum F_y = 0:\quad F_{BC} + 0.6F_{CD} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; -10.5 + 0.6F_{CD} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{CD} = +17.50\,\text{kN}$$

So $F_{CD} = 17.50\,\text{kN}\;T$. (Then $\sum F_x = 0$ gives $F_{CE} = 44.6 - 0.8(17.5) = 30.6\,\text{kN}\;T$, and joint $E$ shows $DE$ is a zero-force member.)

questions.prompt: Using the method of joints, determine the force in member $CF$ of the truss shown ($900\,\text{N}$ horizontal loads at $A$ and $C$; pin at $E$, roller at $F$). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{N}$.
questions.solution:
Diagonals $AD$ and $CF$ span $3\,\text{m}$ horizontally and $2.25\,\text{m}$ vertically, so they have length $3.75\,\text{m}$ and direction cosines $0.8$, $0.6$.

**Joint A** (members $AC$, $AD$; load $900\,\text{N}\rightarrow$):

$$\xrightarrow{+}\sum F_x = 0:\; 900 + 0.8F_{AD} = 0 \Rightarrow F_{AD} = -1125\,\text{N};\qquad +\!\uparrow\sum F_y = 0:\; -F_{AC} - 0.6(-1125) = 0 \Rightarrow F_{AC} = 675\,\text{N}\;T$$

**Joint D:** $\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow F_{CD} = -0.8F_{AD} = 900\,\text{N}\;T$.

**Joint C** (members $CA$, $CD$, $CE$, $CF$; load $900\,\text{N}\rightarrow$):

$$\xrightarrow{+}\sum F_x = 0:\quad 900 + F_{CD} + 0.8F_{CF} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 900 + 900 + 0.8F_{CF} = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{CF} = -2250\,\text{N}$$

So $F_{CF} = 2250\,\text{N}\;C$.

questions.prompt: In the truss shown, which members can be identified as **zero-force members** by inspection, without any calculation?
questions.solution:
Joint $B$ connects only two members, $BA$ (horizontal) and $BD$ (vertical), and carries **no external load**. Two non-collinear members at an unloaded joint must both be zero-force members. So $F_{AB} = F_{BD} = 0$, which agrees with the standard answer.

The other choices are loaded members: $F_{AC} = 675\,\text{N}\;T$, $F_{CE} = 2025\,\text{N}\;T$, $F_{CD} = 900\,\text{N}\;T$, $F_{DF} = 675\,\text{N}\;C$, $F_{EF} = 1800\,\text{N}\;T$.

questions.prompt: Determine the force in member $FH$ of the truss shown (four panels at $2.4\,\text{m} = 9.6\,\text{m}$, depth $1.8\,\text{m}$; $12\,\text{kN}$ loads at $E$ and $G$; pin at $B$, roller at $J$). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
**Reactions.** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_B = 0$: $J(9.6) - 12(4.8) - 12(7.2) = 0 \Rightarrow J = 15.0\,\text{kN}\uparrow$.

**Section** through $EG$, $FG$, $FH$; use the right-hand portion. $EG$ and $FG$ both pass through $G$, so take moments about $G$. $J$ lies $2.4\,\text{m}$ to the right of $G$, and $FH$ lies $1.8\,\text{m}$ below $G$. With $\mathbf{F}_{FH}$ drawn as a tension (pointing left, toward $F$):

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_G = 0:\quad (15.0)(2.4) - F_{FH}(1.8) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{FH} = +20.0\,\text{kN}$$

So $F_{FH} = 20.0\,\text{kN}\;T$. (Also $\sum F_y = 0$: $15 - 12 - 0.6F_{FG} = 0 \Rightarrow F_{FG} = 5.00\,\text{kN}\;T$.)

questions.prompt: Determine the force in member $CE$ of the truss shown ($36\,\text{kN}$ to the left at $A$; $20\,\text{kN}$ down at $D$ and $G$; roller at $B$, pin at $K$; panels $4.5\,\text{m}$, depth $2.4\,\text{m}$). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
**Reaction at B.** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_K = 0$: $-B(13.5) + 36(2.4) + 20(9) + 20(4.5) = 0 \Rightarrow B = 26.4\,\text{kN}\uparrow$.

**Section** through $AD$, $CD$, $CE$ (just left of $D$); use the portion $ABC$. The diagonals $CD$ and $CE$ have length $\sqrt{2.25^2 + 1.2^2} = 2.55\,\text{m}$, with components $(0.8824,\,\pm 0.4706)$.

$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_C = 0$: $-1.2F_{AD} + 1.2(36) - 2.25(26.4) = 0 \Rightarrow F_{AD} = -13.5\,\text{kN}$ ($13.50\,\text{kN}\;C$).

$$\xrightarrow{+}\sum F_x = 0:\; F_{AD} - 36 + 0.8824(F_{CD} + F_{CE}) = 0 \Rightarrow F_{CD} + F_{CE} = 56.1$$

$$+\!\uparrow\sum F_y = 0:\; 26.4 + 0.4706(F_{CD} - F_{CE}) = 0 \Rightarrow F_{CD} - F_{CE} = -56.1$$

Hence $F_{CD} = 0$ and $F_{CE} = +56.1\,\text{kN}$, so $F_{CE} = 56.1\,\text{kN}\;T$.

questions.prompt: Determine the force in member $DG$ of the truss shown, using section $aa$ ($5\,\text{kN}$ horizontal loads at $A$, $D$, $G$; panels $3\,\text{m}$ high, truss $4\,\text{m}$ wide). Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
Section $aa$ cuts **four** members: $DG$, $DE$, $EF$, $FI$. Use the upper portion $ABCDF$. Members $DE$ and $EF$ lie on the horizontal line through $F$, and $FI$ passes through $F$. So a moment equation about $F$ contains only $F_{DG}$.

Take $F$ as origin: $A$ is at $(-4,\,3)$ and $D$ at $(-4,\,0)$. $\mathbf{F}_{DG}$ (tension) pulls $D$ downward.

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_F = 0:\quad -(5)(3) - (5)(0) + F_{DG}(4) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{DG} = +3.75\,\text{kN}$$

So $F_{DG} = 3.75\,\text{kN}\;T$. (About $D$, the same portion gives $F_{FI} = 3.75\,\text{kN}\;C$.)

questions.prompt: For the truss of Probs. 6.63 and 6.64 (shown), determine the force in member $GJ$, using section $bb$. Determine the magnitude of the force in $\text{kN}$.
questions.solution:
Section $bb$ cuts $GJ$, $GH$, $HI$, $IK$. $GH$ and $HI$ lie on the horizontal line through $I$, and $IK$ passes through $I$, so take moments about $I$ for the upper portion.

With $I$ as origin, the $5\text{-kN}$ loads act at $A(-4,\,6)$, $D(-4,\,3)$, $G(-4,\,0)$, and $\mathbf{F}_{GJ}$ (tension) pulls $G$ downward at $x = -4$:

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_I = 0:\quad -(5)(6) - (5)(3) - (5)(0) + F_{GJ}(4) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F_{GJ} = +11.25\,\text{kN}$$

So $F_{GJ} = 11.25\,\text{kN}\;T$ (and, about $G$, $F_{IK} = 11.25\,\text{kN}\;C$).

questions.prompt: Classify each of the structures (a), (b), (c) shown as completely, partially, or improperly constrained; if completely constrained, further classify as determinate or indeterminate. (All members can act in tension and compression.)

options.label: A
options.text: (a) completely constrained, determinate; (b) partially constrained; (c) improperly constrained

options.label: B
options.text: (a) completely constrained, indeterminate; (b) partially constrained; (c) completely constrained, determinate

options.label: C
options.text: (a) partially constrained; (b) completely constrained, determinate; (c) improperly constrained

options.label: D
options.text: (a) completely constrained, determinate; (b) improperly constrained; (c) partially constrained

questions.solution:
Each truss has $n = 10$ joints, so $2n = 20$.

- **(a)** $m = 16$ (the second panel has no diagonal), with a pin plus two rollers, so $r = 4$. Then $m + r = 20 = 2n$, and the reactions and member forces can all be found (the middle roller supplies the shear of the open panel). **Completely constrained, determinate.**
- **(b)** $m = 16$, with a pin and one roller, so $r = 3$. Then $m + r = 19 < 2n$: **partially constrained**.
- **(c)** $m = 17$, with a pin and a horizontal link, so $r = 3$. The counts match, $m + r = 20$, but the link's line of action passes through the pin: the reactions are concurrent, so the truss is **improperly constrained** ($m + r = 2n$ is necessary, not sufficient).

questions.prompt: In the frame shown ($AB$ horizontal $80\,\text{mm}$, then $BC$ to $C$, $170\,\text{mm}$ further right and $125\,\text{mm}$ lower; $D$ below $B$ at the level of $C$; $E$ $75\,\text{mm}$ below $C$ on the wall), a $750\text{-N}$ force directed vertically downward is applied **at $B$**. Determine the vertical component $A_y$ of the reaction at $A$ (in $\text{N}$; it acts upward).
questions.solution:
With the load at $B$, member $EDC$ is a **two-force member**, so the force at $C$ acts along $EC$. Take $A$ as origin: $B(80,\,0)$, $C(250,\,-125)$, $E(0,\,-200)$. Then $EC$ has direction $(250,\,75)$.

Let the force that $EDC$ exerts on $ABC$ at $C$ be $k(250,\,75)/261.0$.

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_A = 0:\quad -750(80) + 250\Big(\tfrac{75k}{261}\Big) + 125\Big(\tfrac{250k}{261}\Big) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; k = 313\,\text{N}$$

So the force at $C$ has components $(300,\,90)\,\text{N}$, and $E_x = 300\,\text{N}\rightarrow$, $E_y = 90.0\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

**Member ABC:** $\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow A_x = 300\,\text{N}\leftarrow$. $\;\sum F_y = 0$: $A_y - 750 + 90 = 0 \Rightarrow A_y = 660\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

questions.prompt: For the frame shown, the $750\text{-N}$ downward force is now applied **at $D$** instead of $B$. Which set of reaction components is correct?
questions.solution:
Now $ABC$ is the **two-force member**, so the force at $C$ acts along $AC$, direction $(250,\,-125)$. Take $E$ as origin for member $EDC$: $D(80,\,75)$, $C(250,\,75)$. Let the force on $EDC$ at $C$ be $k(250,\,-125)/279.5$.

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_E = 0:\quad -750(80) + 250\Big(-\tfrac{125k}{279.5}\Big) - 75\Big(\tfrac{250k}{279.5}\Big) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; k = -335.4\,\text{N}$$

So $EDC$ is pulled at $C$ by $(-300,\,+150)\,\text{N}$: $ABC$ is in tension. Then $A_x = 300\,\text{N}\leftarrow$ and $A_y = 150.0\,\text{N}\uparrow$. On $EDC$: $E_x = 300\,\text{N}\rightarrow$ and $E_y = 750 - 150 = 600\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

Choice B is the answer for the load at $B$. C has the senses reversed. D wrongly ignores the horizontal components.

questions.prompt: Knowing that the pulley has a radius of $0.5\,\text{m}$, determine the horizontal component $A_x$ of the reaction at $A$ for the frame shown ($700\text{-N}$ load hung from the cable). Give the magnitude in $\text{N}$ (it acts to the left).
questions.solution:
Coordinates with $A$ at the origin: $B(0,\,2)$, $C(1,\,3)$, $E(7,\,0)$. The pulley centre $D(4,\,1.5)$ lies on $CE$. The cable runs horizontally from $B$ to the top of the pulley ($y = 2$) and leaves vertically at $x = 4.5\,\text{m}$, carrying $700\,\text{N}$.

**Entire frame** (cable segment $BD$ internal): $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_A = 0$: $E_y(7) - 700(4.5) = 0 \Rightarrow E_y = 450\,\text{N}\uparrow$, so $A_y = 700 - 450 = 250\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

**Member ABC** (forces at $A$, the cable pull of $700\,\text{N}$ to the right at $B$, and the pin $C$):

$$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_C = 0:\quad -A_y(1) + A_x(3) + 700(1) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; -250 + 3A_x + 700 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; A_x = -150\,\text{N}$$

So $A_x = 150.0\,\text{N}\leftarrow$ (and $E_x = 150.0\,\text{N}\rightarrow$).

questions.prompt: For the frame and loading shown ($12\,\text{kN}$ down at $D$), determine the horizontal component $E_x$ of the force acting on member $ABE$ at $E$. Give the magnitude in $\text{kN}$ (it acts to the left).
questions.solution:
Coordinates: $E(0,0)$, $F(1.8,0)$, $A(0.9,\,1.8)$. Bar $BCD$ is at $y = 0.6$, with $B(0.3,\,0.6)$ on $AE$, $C(1.5,\,0.6)$ on $AF$ and $D(2.1,\,0.6)$. The pin at $C$ rides in a slot along $AF$, so the force at $C$ is **perpendicular to $AF$**, along $(0.894,\,0.447)$.

**Bar BCD:** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_B = 0$: $1.2(0.447c) - 12(1.8) = 0 \Rightarrow c = 40.25\,\text{kN}$, so $\mathbf{C} = (36,\,18)\,\text{kN}$. Then $\sum F = 0$ gives a force on $BCD$ at $B$ of $(-36,\,-6)$. The force **on $ABE$** at $B$ is therefore $36.0\,\text{kN}\rightarrow$, $6.00\,\text{kN}\uparrow$.

**Entire frame:** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_E = 0$: $F_y(1.8) - 12(2.1) = 0 \Rightarrow F_y = 14\,\text{kN}$, so $E_y = -2.00\,\text{kN}$ ($\downarrow$).

**Member ABE:** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_A = 0$: $(-0.6)(6) - (-1.2)(36) + (-0.9)(-2) - (-1.8)E_x = 0 \Rightarrow 41.4 + 1.8E_x = 0 \Rightarrow E_x = -23.0\,\text{kN}$.

So $E_x = 23.0\,\text{kN}\leftarrow$ (then $A_x = 13.00\,\text{kN}\leftarrow$, $A_y = 4.00\,\text{kN}\downarrow$).

questions.prompt: The axis of the three-hinge arch $ABC$ is a parabola with vertex at $B$. Knowing that $P = 112\,\text{kN}$ and $Q = 140\,\text{kN}$, determine the horizontal component $A_x$ of the reaction at $A$ (in $\text{kN}$; it acts to the right).
questions.solution:
Coordinates: $A(0,0)$, $B(8,\,3.2)$, $C(14,\,1.4)\,\text{m}$. $P$ acts at $x = 5\,\text{m}$ on $AB$ and $Q$ at $x = 11\,\text{m}$ on $BC$. The arch is not rigid without its supports, so we need free bodies of the parts.

**Entire arch:** $\sum F_x = 0 \Rightarrow C_x = -A_x$. $\;+\circlearrowleft\sum M_A = 0$: $14C_y - 1.4C_x - 112(5) - 140(11) = 0 \Rightarrow 14C_y + 1.4A_x = 2100$.

**Segment BC:** $+\circlearrowleft\sum M_B = 0$: $6C_y + 1.8C_x - 140(3) = 0 \Rightarrow 6C_y - 1.8A_x = 420 \Rightarrow C_y = 70 + 0.3A_x$.

Substituting: $14(70 + 0.3A_x) + 1.4A_x = 2100 \Rightarrow 5.6A_x = 1120 \Rightarrow A_x = 200\,\text{kN}\rightarrow$.

Then $C_y = 130\,\text{kN}$ and $A_y = 252 - 130 = 122.0\,\text{kN}\uparrow$. On $AB$ at $B$: $B_x = 200\,\text{kN}\leftarrow$, $B_y = 10.00\,\text{kN}\downarrow$.

questions.prompt: The telescoping arm $ABC$ provides an elevated platform; the workers and platform have a mass of $200\,\text{kg}$ with combined centre of gravity directly above $C$ ($AC = 5\,\text{m}$, $AB = 2.4\,\text{m}$; $D$ is $0.9\,\text{m}$ below and $0.5\,\text{m}$ behind $A$). For $\theta = 20^\circ$, determine the magnitude of the force exerted at $B$ by the single hydraulic cylinder $BD$ (in $\text{kN}$).
questions.solution:
$W = (200)(9.81) = 1962\,\text{N}$. Take $A$ as origin, with the arm inclined at $20^\circ$:

- $C = (-5\cos 20^\circ,\ 5\sin 20^\circ) = (-4.698,\,1.710)$
- $B = (-2.4\cos 20^\circ,\ 2.4\sin 20^\circ) = (-2.255,\,0.821)$
- $D = (-0.5,\,-0.9)$

$\overrightarrow{DB} = (-1.755,\,1.721)$, of length $2.458\,\text{m}$, so the unit vector is $(-0.7141,\,0.7001)$ (inclined at $44.4^\circ$). $BD$ is a two-force member pushing on the arm along $DB$.

**Free body ABC**, $\sum M_A = 0$:

$$(-4.698)(-1962) + F_{BD}\big[(-2.255)(0.7001) - (0.821)(-0.7141)\big] = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 9218 - 0.9927F_{BD} = 0$$

$$F_{BD} = 9286\,\text{N} = 9.29\,\text{kN}\ \text{at}\ 44.4^\circ$$

(Then $\sum F = 0$ gives $\mathbf{A} = 8.04\,\text{kN}$ at $34.4^\circ$.)
